title: Why Automated QC Outperforms Manual Editing on Consistency
use_cases: Use when performing systematic consistency checks across long-form manuscripts
Implement when world rules need precise enforcement across large volumes of text
Configure when scaling quality control from short stories to epic-length novels
Use when identifying vulnerable narrative points through an automated QC report
Implement when maintaining a dynamic inventory of character details and world-building facts
content:
A human editor is excellent for style, tone, and nuance. But for systematic consistency checks across hundreds of pages, automated QC has clear advantages:

- Completeness: The QC checks every scene against every relevant detail in the inventory. No human can do that by Chapter 50.
- Speed: The check takes seconds, not days.
- Objectivity: No fatigue, no attention gaps, no "nobody will notice."
- Scalability: Whether 10 chapters or 100 — the effort stays the same.

This doesn't replace an editor. It complements one. Your editor can focus on craft because the facts already check out.

1. Define your world rules precisely — the clearer your rules, the better the QC can enforce them
2. Maintain your inventory — update character descriptions when things change
3. Take warnings seriously — they're not errors, but often an early warning signal for later problems
4. Use the QC report — it shows you where your novel is most vulnerable to inconsistencies
